expectations.text: A spec for the overdue feature exists under OUTPUT_DIR/repo/docs/product-specs/, either as a new file with a new prefix or as new criteria appended to tickets.md or cli.md with fresh IDs; the transcript or spec says which was chosen and why.
expectations.evidence: Amended tickets.md (TKT-014..TKT-017) and cli.md (CLI-010..CLI-013; CLI-001 and CLI-006 amended). Final message: 'I amended two spec files and created none, because the repo keeps one spec file per feature area.'

expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph: 'Support agents need to see which tickets missed their due time, so they can work on those first. A ticket that is still unresolved after its due time from TKT-005 is overdue.' File keeps 'Prefix: `TKT`.'. 'Out of scope for this feature:' lists 5 boundaries (no new state or event kind, no alerts/notifications, no due-time/lateness display, no filters, no change to TKT-005 hours or business-hours SLA).

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 8 new criteria from the diff: TKT-014, TKT-015, TKT-016, TKT-017, CLI-010, CLI-011, CLI-012, CLI-013. All correctly headed, zero-padded, unique, testable_lines=0. CLI-010 (4 sentences + example + TODO) and CLI-011 (5 sentences) are longer than typical.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-010 '`OVERDUE` in place of its state' with example '#3 [P1] OVERDUE  Printer on fire'. Filter: CLI-011 'Tickets that are not overdue do not appear.' Order: TKT-017 'sorted by due time ascending... same due time... ID ascending'. Exact due: TKT-014 'At the exact due time, the ticket is not overdue yet' (+ TODO). Closed: TKT-015 'A `closed` ticket is never overdue' (+ TODO). Empty: CLI-011 'With no overdue tickets, the command prints nothing and exits with code 0.' Stated as a criterion, not only as an assumption.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0). Outcomes described as printed lines, stdout, usage errors and exit codes.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: 'Overdue is a condition, not a state. The help desk computes it from the current time each time a command runs. It never records overdue in the log. Thus TKT-001, LOG-002, LOG-009, and INV-001 stay true without change.' TKT-016: 'No event is appended... the log file does not change.' Non-goals exclude a new event kind. INV-002 not cited by ID, but no log write is proposed.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-014 reuses 'its due time from TKT-005'. CLI-010 states explicitly: 'The list order stays the ID order of TKT-013.' TKT-017 adds 'Due order can differ from ID order.'

expectations.text: docs/product-specs/README.md is updated: the new file appears in the prefix table and the index with a one-line summary (or, if criteria were appended to an existing file, the README needed no change and the spec says so).
